Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the final innings of this Test to get underway! The umpires make their way back out to the middle as the Indian players are seen standing in a circle near the boundary rope before walking onto the field as well. It will be the duo of Shadman Islam and Zakir Hasan to open the innings for Bangladesh. Jasprit Bumrah has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

Right then, twins tons from Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant followed by a quick cameo from KL Rahul and India have piled on a lead of over 500 runs quite quickly. Bangladesh need 515 runs to pull off an unlikely win with more than two days remaining in the match whereas Jasprit Bumrah and co will be looking to do what they did in the first innings. The run chase is up next, so, don't go anywhere.

Bangladesh have been made to toil in the field not long but certainly very hard as the pitch really didn't have anything in it and they barely had any answer to India's counter-attacking batting. Mehidy Hasan was the only bowler on Day 3 who looked like picking up a wicket and got rid of Rishabh Pant but the damage had already been done. It will now be nearly impossible for the batters of Bangladesh to get it done in the fourth innings with the bat.

There's that declaration! Rohit Sharma signals from the dressing room and India declare on 287/4 on the back of a couple of stellar tons from Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant. This means they have a lead of 514 runs to play in the final innings with and we are only midway through this Test match.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 3! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of Bangladesh. Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant are also back out to resume their stay at the crease. It will be Mehidy Hasan to begin proceedings with the ball after the break. Let's play...
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

Right then, India's lead is already up to 432 runs and they still have 7 wickets in hand. With there still no sign of spin on the deck, India will look to bat most of the next session and add 100 or so runs to the total. Bangladesh need to be very careful and need a change of plans after the break if they are to cause any trouble to the Indian batters. Join us at 6.40 am GMT for the post-Lunch session.

The second hour of the first session saw a lot more action with both Gill and Pant surpassing the 50-run mark and then towards the end, Pant really opened up his arms and then came a plethora of boundaries. Gill didn't hold back either and hit a few lovely big hits. There was one proper opportunity created by Shakib Al Hasan late in the session but skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto dropped a simple catch to add to Bangladesh's misery.

The first hour of play was more of a sedate one with India playing a few shots in between after which the boundaries dried up as Mehidy Hasan bowled a good holding spell from one end. However, Bangladesh failed to create wicket-taking opportunities and both Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant were able to keep the scoreboard ticking.

A dominating session for India with the bat and they now have complete control of this Test match. There was overnight rain in Chennai and the conditions were overcast to begin with but the Bangladeshi pacers didn't find any lateral movement or swing and the pitch had really flattened out. As many as 124 runs were scored in just 28 overs with most of them coming in the last 10 overs or so.
Drags his length and on middle, Shubman Gill goes back and across, drags it down to long on for a single. And that will be LUNCH ON DAY 3!

Well, the first hour of Day 3 has flown by and fair to say, that India has done well to resist so far, going unblemished. After an initial burst from Gill and Pant both in the first half hour or so, things have slowed down considerably for India since the last few overs, but with wickets in hand, India really won't mind. Commentary.Commentary: Well then, all set for the third day to commence! Conditions are pretty overcast as of now with a cloud cover hovering over Chennai. The umpires walk out to the middle, and the players of Bangladesh spread out to their respective positions as well. Shubman Gill unbeaten on 33 and Rishabh Pant on 12, to resume their innings. And spin to start with, Mehidy Hasan to kick off the proceedings on Day 3. Let's play...

The live pictures from the ground show that there has been some rain in Chennai but the broadcasters have confirmed that Day 3 will start on time which is excellent news. We are just about 20 minutes away from the start, so, stay tuned.

With things turning out at a rapid pace, a result before Day 5 seems highly likely. The first hour of the first session today could well set the tone for the remainder of this intriguing contest. Will India press home their advantage, or can Bangladesh spark a dramatic turnaround? The stage is set for another riveting day of Test cricket. Stay tuned as the first ball isn't far away.

Now, with Bangladesh already staring at a huge target, and the wear and tear of the pitch hinting towards more effectiveness of spin in the next two days, they would really need a solid opening hour to prevent India from running away. Shakib Al Hasan, pretty much ineffective until now with the ball, will surely be more crucial when the ball gets that grip, along with Mehidy Hasan. It’s all about utilizing the conditions well and adapting accordingly.  Their ability to exploit the deteriorating surface might be key to Bangladesh's fightback.

Bangladesh on the other hand, would not be very pleased with how things panned out for them on the second day. Coming out to bowl again after just a 47-over stint with the bat is not that easy. However, a slight ray of hope for them was that they did manage to take three early wickets. Taskin Ahmed looked much improved with his lines and lengths while Nahid Rana has shouldered him well too. But they know, the job is far from done as they come to Day 3, they would expect a strong comeback and aim to restrict India from mounting a huge total on the board. But for that, they need step up collectively as a whole unit.

India might be in a strong position if you look at the scorecard, but they have some issues to address as well. The top order hasn’t contributed much and the bulk of scoring has been done by the middle and lower middle order. However, Shubman Gill resisted strongly after India lost its top three pretty soon. Yes, Virat Kohli not taking the review for that LBW must be itching the team pretty much but that's in the rearview mirror now. Looking forward, with Pant and Gill set to resume their innings, and a long batting depth to follow, India wouldn’t mind batting all day long as there’s a lot of time left in the match. However, it all depends on the first hour or so. If they sustain it without much damage, we could be seeing a total well past 400 as well.

Day two in Chennai was wild! Who would have thought we'd see 17 wickets fall? That's never happened before in a Test here. The fast bowlers grabbed 14 of those wickets. In Chennai of all places, where spinners usually run the show. Bumrah was on fire for India and took a spectacular 4-fer, doing his thing like always. Akash Deep too, showed promise with the cherry. And for Bangladesh, the real wrecker-in-chief was Hasan Mahmud who bagged five wickets to his name. While Taskin Ahmed too, showed huge improvement.

Hello and a very warm welcome to Day 3 of this first Test between India and Bangladesh. It is called a 'Moving Day' by the pundits but this game has moved at a brisk pace and might as well get wrapped up before the fifth day or so, given how things have panned out so far. But as of now, India holds a strong position after taking the broad lead of 308 runs. Whereas, Bangladesh is aiming for a miraculous comeback.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from all the action of Day 2. As the game progresses, Bangladesh faces a steep uphill battle. Their primary objective now will be to contain India's momentum and prevent them from running away with the match while India would be mighty pleased to extend the lead beyond 350 to get in the safe zone. And with the wear and tear of the pitch, with evident roughs at both ends, we might see more effective spin in the remaining days. Day 3, is often known as the 'Moving Day' in any Test, but this one has already moved at a rapid pace. With all said and done, the action on Day 3 begins on Saturday, September 21 at 4 am GMT. Till then, cheers and take care!

Ravindra Jadeja is down for a chat. He says that missing out on the ton is part and parcel of the game but is quite happy with his bowling. Adds that he has a good opportunity to get to 300 Test wickets on this ground but they need to get to above 150 which will put them in a good position with the lead. Reckons that the pitch looks good but there is still something in it for the pacers and they can exploit what is on offer. Goes on to say that the chat with Ashwin while batting was that they would not take many risks with the running and just take the easy single on offer. Ends by saying that there is still a fair bit in it for the bowlers and whether it's a pacer or a spinner, they are in the game.

So, in whose favour is this Test match tilted towards? Of the six sessions played so far, India has convincingly controlled four, including a clean sweep of all three on Day 2. Bangladesh's influence has been limited to just two sessions that too on the opening day. So, it is pretty much clear that India holds a commanding position.

Cut to the third innings, India too, started off with a bit of a struggle as they lost both openers inside the first ten overs. However, the cushion of a substantial lead allowed them to weather this early storm. Gill and Kohli rose to the occasion, forming a resilient partnership for the third wicket. The duo showcased their skill with a series of elegant strokes, effectively steadying the innings with a 39-run stand. But eventually, Virat Kohli perished right on the cusp of the stumps throwing away a good start. And in the end, Rishabh Pant and Shubman Gill saw India through the day. Bangladesh on the other hand, managed to take three wickets, with Taskin Ahmed, Nahid Rana and Mehidy Hasan each claiming one.

India on the other hand, were almost flawless with whatever they did with the ball in hand in the second and the third sessions. Following a dominant performance in the second session, the bowlers didn't waste much time cleaning up the tail of Bangladesh as Bumrah and Siraj took one apiece to bundle the opposition on a low score and a healthy lead of 227 runs. Bumrah was the pick of the bowlers as he snagged a sensational 4-fer and the others chipped in with wickets as well. A rarity in Chennai, Ashwin remained wicketless but fairly to the spinners, there wasn't much help from the pitch as yet, but they did well enough to tie the opposition for runs.

As the final session began, Bangladesh was already in dire straits, having lost eight wickets and managing only a paltry 112 runs. Their key batters failed to make a significant impact despite favourable batting conditions. Mehidy Hasan's contribution of 27 runs came under constant pressure and proved insufficient to turn the tide. Only four batters managed to surpass the 20-run mark, with Shakib and Mehidy emerging as the top scorers. Ultimately, Bangladesh crumbled under the extreme pressure exerted by the bowlers, unable to mount a substantial resistance.

Cleverly bowled by Mehidy Hasan as he darts this one in full and quick around off, Kohli looks to get a stride across and play across the line but ends up playing all around it. The ball pings him in front of off stump and the finger is raised. The only question was of the impact which seems to be in line and Kohli throws away a decent start as he departs for 17 (37). India are now 67/3 with a lead of 294 runs. But surprisingly, the replay later on shows that there was indeed a spike when the ball passed close to the bat. Although, it is not yet sure whether the spike was off the bat in contact with the ground or with the ball. The only person who would've known about the nick was Virat Kohli but he didn't opt for a review. A huge moment in the game, and everyone in the dugout is in a state of shock including Gill on the crease after seeing it on the giant screen.
